A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRASS architecture. Their full text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v3 reports original GRASS benchmark results, component ablations, runtime measurements and variability analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds a fixed-rewiring ablation and an eight-run evaluation on roman-empire.

M1.justification: The encoding, random rewiring, attention, edge flipping and pooling procedures remain unchanged. The GLU task-head activation is newly documented, while edge-encoding batch normalization was already present in v3 Equation 2. Fixed rewiring is an added experimental control.

E1.justification: v4 Appendix C adds evaluation on roman-empire, extending coverage to a single heterophilic graph. All nine previously evaluated benchmark datasets remain.

E2.justification: The new roman-empire comparison includes NAGphormer and Polynormer, which were absent from v3's comparisons, and reports GAT (-sep). Comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 adds a ZINC control that rewires once before training instead of every epoch. Its new roman-empire configuration uses 2,075,730 parameters, 24 attention layers, 4,000 epochs and batch size one (Table 13). Previously reported benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a controlled test of whether repeatedly resampling added edges matters, complementing the existing tests of edge count and regularity. Previous encoding, attention and other design ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Existing run counts, repeated test evaluations, standard deviations and standard-error reporting are unchanged. The added ablation and roman-empire results use the established mean-plus-standard-deviation practice over eight runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds ZINC MAE of 0.0645 ± 0.0015 for fixed rewiring, versus 0.0470 ± 0.0013 for resampling. New Table 5 reports roman-empire accuracy of 91.34 ± 0.22, below NeuralWalker and Polynormer. Existing numerical results are unchanged; Section 4.2 additionally reports, without numerical results, that D-RRWP underperforms RRWP on Peptides-struct.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the scalar D-RRWP reconstruction expression by taking the dot product with diag(Lambda^h), rather than the diagonal matrix Lambda^h itself. This is a limited mathematical correction; the underlying approximation, complexity bounds and Appendix A arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about combining encoding, rewiring and additive attention. The highlighted 20.3% ZINC MAE reduction is unchanged; the additional experiments do not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies D-RRWP's applicability by acknowledging weaker performance on Peptides-struct. It interprets the new rewiring control as evidence that resampling, alongside regularity, matters for performance. Section 5.1 also clarifies deterministic-output handling through an input-graph hash.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 replaces a promised future code release with a stated repository location. Appendix F newly specifies GLU activation in task-head hidden layers and supplies roman-empire hyperparameters. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the existing implementation.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Dauphin et al. for GLU, Platonov et al. for heterophilic evaluation, Zhou et al. for joint node-edge representations, and Zehui et al. to distinguish DropAttention. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 locally revises the introduction, mathematical explanations, attention discussion and limitations. It adds acknowledgments and a heterophily appendix, renumbers subsequent appendices, and updates the publication header. The main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the roman-empire results table, expands Table 4 and the final hyperparameter table, and revises captions and table sizing. Existing Figures 1–5 are retained, with limited page reflow and appendix-table renumbering.

improvement.justification: The fixed-rewiring control strengthens evidence for the value of resampling, while roman-empire modestly broadens empirical coverage. The D-RRWP qualification, task-head details and concrete code location improve transparency. These are useful, limited gains over v3; the core method and principal results remain unchanged.
